# Platform hardening

> Security baselines and hardening guidance for Windows, Linux, macOS, and mobile devices.

Part of the [domain list](README.md). 44 resources in 5 sections. Managing fleets of devices sits in Endpoint and device management; framework-level control catalogs sit in GRC and security program.

For references, how-to guides, and learning paths on this subject, see the TeamStarWolf library's [matching domain page](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/hubs/platform-hardening.md).

## Baselines and benchmarks

Which published baseline should this system meet?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Device security guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/device-security-guidance) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | NCSC device guides in one collection, with groups including platform guides, getting ready, policies and settings, managing deployed devices, infrastructure, and bring your own device. | Reference | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-190](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/190/final) | NIST | Explains container technology, risks to images, registries, orchestrators, containers, and host operating systems, countermeasures for those risks, threat scenarios, and security across the life cycle. | Standard | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/124/r2/final) | NIST | Covers mobile device characteristics, threats to devices and their management systems, device-side and enterprise security technologies, mitigations, and the deployment life cycle through disposal. | Standard | Free |
| [Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs)](https://www.cyber.mil/stigs/) | Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) | Home of the DoD's Security Requirements Guides and STIGs, with a document library that includes SCAP benchmarks, automation content, Group Policy Objects, and library compilations. | Standard | Free |
| [National Checklist Program Checklist Repository](https://ncp.nist.gov/repository) | NIST | Searchable repository of security configuration checklists, filtered by keyword, type, issuing authority, target product, content type, and tool compatibility, with download links. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [CIS Benchmarks](https://www.cisecurity.org/cis-benchmarks) | Center for Internet Security | Consensus configuration recommendations for many vendor product families, used as hardening baselines. | Standard | Free with account |

Listed here from another domain: CIS Benchmarks ([GRC and security program](grc-and-security-program.md#frameworks-controls-and-benchmarks)).

## Windows hardening

How do I harden Windows clients and servers?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Security baselines guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/windows-security-baselines) | Microsoft | Microsoft's guide to Windows security baselines, including what a baseline is, principles behind the settings, and where to get them, by download or through Intune. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit - How to use](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/security-compliance-toolkit-10) | Microsoft | Microsoft's page on the Security Compliance Toolkit, with sections on its tools: Policy Analyzer, LGPO, Set Object Security, and GPO to Policy Rules. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Windows Security documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/) | Microsoft | Windows security hub: overview with a downloadable guide, hardware security, operating system security, application and agent security, identity protection, cloud services, security foundation, and privacy. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Attack surface reduction (ASR) rules reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference) | Microsoft | Reference to Defender's attack surface reduction rules: operating system and deployment method support, alerts and notifications, then details of standard protection rules and the others. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Application Control for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's App Control for Business and AppLocker documentation, grouped into overview, policy design, policy configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Microsoft recommended driver block rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules) | Microsoft | Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist: when Windows enforces it, blocking the listed drivers with App Control, download and apply steps, and the blocklist as XML. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [BitLocker device encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's overview of BitLocker, including BitLocker To Go, its use of the TPM, system and licensing requirements, and how device encryption differs. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Credential Guard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's overview of Credential Guard: where it is on by default on Windows and Windows Server, and its hardware and software, licensing, and application requirements. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Protect devices from exploits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/exploit-protection) | Microsoft | Microsoft's page on Windows exploit protection: supported versions, its events in the Defender portal, advanced hunting, and Event Viewer, and a comparison of mitigations. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [System audit policy recommendations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/audit-policy-recommendations) | Microsoft | Microsoft's audit policy page, including recommendations by operating system, setting the policy, events to monitor, and which Active Directory objects to watch. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [HardeningKitty](https://github.com/scipag/HardeningKitty) | scip AG | Runs finding lists against Windows in modes: Audit scores the system, Config reads its settings, HailMary applies a list, and GPO builds a Group Policy. | Tool | Free |
| [Harden Windows Security](https://github.com/HotCakeX/Harden-Windows-Security) | Violet Hansen (HotCakeX) | Repository for two Windows apps, Harden System Security and AppControl Manager, with README sections including Microsoft Store installation, rationale, security recommendations, and a roadmap. | Tool | Free |
| [Windows LAPS overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview) | Microsoft | Introduces Windows LAPS for managing local administrator passwords: supported platforms, use with Microsoft Entra ID, policy settings, and migration from legacy Microsoft LAPS. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Linux and container hardening

How do I harden a Linux host and the containers on it?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Ubuntu Security Guide (USG)](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/compliance/usg/) | Canonical | Canonical's documentation for the USG tool: available profiles, installation through the Ubuntu Pro client, and separate guides for CIS and DISA STIG compliance. | Vendor documentation | Freemium |
| [SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP7 Security and Hardening Guide](https://documentation.suse.com/sles/15-SP7/html/SLES-all/book-security.html) | SUSE | SUSE's guide for SLES 15 SP7, in parts including authentication, local security, network security, regulations and compliance, and confining privileges with AppArmor. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Security - ArchWiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Security) | Arch Linux | ArchWiki's Security article, with sections including passwords, storage, user setup, mandatory access control, kernel hardening, sandboxing applications, and network and firewalls. | Reference | Free |
| [Kernel Self-Protection Project: Recommended Settings](https://kspp.github.io/Recommended_Settings) | Kernel Self-Protection Project | The Kernel Self-Protection Project's list of hardening settings for a Linux kernel: build CONFIG options by architecture, kernel command line options, and sysctls. | Reference | Free |
| [kernel-hardening-checker](https://github.com/a13xp0p0v/kernel-hardening-checker) (formerly kconfig-hardened-check) | Alexander Popov (a13xp0p0v) | Compares a kernel's Kconfig file, command line, and sysctl settings with hardening recommendations; README sections include output modes, Kconfig fragment generation, and questions and answers. | Tool | Free |
| [The SELinux Notebook](https://github.com/SELinuxProject/selinux-notebook) | SELinux Project | SELinux reference kept as Markdown in a repository: read it on GitHub, download a pre-built release, or build your own EPUB, PDF, or HTML copy. | Reference | Free |
| [AppArmor Documentation](https://apparmor.net/) | AppArmor project (Canonical) | AppArmor's official documentation: getting started, writing and managing profiles, troubleshooting and monitoring, and background pages including a comparison with SELinux, with notes on recent releases. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [OpenSSH guidelines](https://infosec.mozilla.org/guidelines/openssh) | Mozilla | Mozilla's OpenSSH settings by profile, including modern and intermediate server and client configurations, multi-factor authentication, cipher and algorithm choices, key generation, and key protection. | Reference | Free |
| [SSH Hardening Guides](https://www.ssh-audit.com/hardening_guides.html) | Positron Security | Step-by-step SSH hardening commands for named systems and releases, in server, client, community-developed, and legacy groups. | Reference | Free |
| [Fail2Ban](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban) | Fail2Ban | Blocks the source of repeated failed logins to services such as sshd for a set time; README includes installation, configuration, documentation links, and contact channels. | Tool | Free |
| [AIDE - Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment](https://aide.github.io/) | AIDE | File integrity checker that compares files with a stored database of attributes and digests; the site includes features, packages, signed source downloads, and help channels. | Tool | Free |
| [USBGuard](https://usbguard.github.io/) | USBGuard | Allows or blocks USB devices on Linux by rule, through kernel device authorization: a daemon, rule language, command-line and GUI interfaces, and C++ API. | Tool | Free |
| [Docker Engine security](https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/) | Docker Inc | Docker's review of Engine security: kernel namespaces, control groups, the daemon's attack surface, Linux capabilities, content trust signature verification, and other kernel security features. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Docker Bench for Security](https://github.com/docker/docker-bench-security) | Docker | Script that tests a Docker host and its containers against the CIS Docker Benchmark; runs from the host or as a container. | Tool | Free |
| [Kubernetes Security Checklist](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/security-checklist/) | Kubernetes | Checklist from Kubernetes documentation with items grouped under network security, authentication and authorization, secrets, images, pod security and placement, admission controllers, and logs and auditing. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [kube-bench](https://github.com/aquasecurity/kube-bench) | Aqua Security | Checks a Kubernetes cluster against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, with tests defined in YAML and job files for EKS, AKS, GKE, and other managed services. | Tool | Free |

## macOS and mobile hardening

How do I harden Macs, iPhones, and Android devices?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [macOS Security Compliance Project](https://pages.nist.gov/macos_security/) | NIST | Documentation for mSCP on visionOS, iPadOS, iOS, and macOS: how-to guides for generating baselines, guidance, configuration profiles, and compliance scripts, a repository reference, and FAQ. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [Apple Platform Security](https://support.apple.com/guide/security/welcome/web) | Apple | Apple's guide to the security of its devices, with chapters including hardware security, app security, system security, services security, and encryption and Data Protection. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [macOS Security and Privacy Guide](https://github.com/drduh/macOS-Security-and-Privacy-Guide) | drduh | Single-page guide in a repository, with sections including threat model, FileVault, Lockdown Mode, firewall, DNS, browsers, and malware, for Apple silicon Macs. | Reference | Free |
| [Objective-See's Tools](https://objective-see.org/tools.html) | Objective-See Foundation | Download page for Mac tools, including the LuLu firewall, BlockBlock and KnockKnock for persistence, ReiKey for keyboard event taps, and Netiquette for network connections. | Tool | Free |
| [About Lockdown Mode](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105120) | Apple | Apple's article on Lockdown Mode, including what it restricts, how to enable it on iPhone, iPad, or Mac, and excluding websites, apps, or contacts. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Android security features](https://source.android.com/docs/security/features) | Google (Android Open Source Project) | Android Open Source Project summary of platform security features, including Verified Boot, the Trusty TEE, SELinux, Keystore, encryption, biometrics, authentication, app signing, and application sandbox. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [GrapheneOS features overview](https://grapheneos.org/features) | GrapheneOS Foundation | GrapheneOS's feature list for its hardened Android-based phone OS, including exploit mitigations, sandboxed Google Play, network and sensor permission toggles, and Storage Scopes. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Audit and assessment tools

How do I measure a host against a baseline?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Lynis](https://cisofy.com/lynis/) | CISOfy | Introduction to the Lynis audit tool, with sections including supported operating systems, audit steps, tests, plugins, supported standards, and installation; Lynis Enterprise is paid. | Tool | Freemium |
| [ComplianceAsCode content](https://github.com/ComplianceAsCode/content) | ComplianceAsCode | Security policy content, with README sections including installation from packages, release ZIPs, or source, and usage with oscap, SCAP Workbench, oscap-ssh, Ansible, and Bash. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [DevSec Hardening Framework](https://dev-sec.io/) | DevSec Hardening Framework Team | Hardening baselines for servers and services, including Linux, SSH, Docker, MySQL, and Nginx, as InSpec profiles, most with remediation code for Ansible, Chef, or Puppet. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [Goss](https://github.com/goss-org/goss) | goss-org | Server validation tool whose README includes installation, a quick start that writes an sshd test, supported resources and output formats, a container image, and limitations. | Tool | Free |
| [Best Practice Auditd Configuration](https://github.com/Neo23x0/auditd) | Florian Roth (Neo23x0) | An audit.rules file for the Linux audit daemon, with README sections including coverage, related projects, validation, the UID_MIN setting, and sources. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [OpenSCAP](https://www.open-scap.org/) | Red Hat | Tools for scanning a system against a chosen security policy and evaluating its compliance with standards. | Tool | Free |
